openings.claim: A detachable wire bridle may retain by tension and keep the plate recoverable: replace magnetic attraction with flexible connections between unmarked plate-body loops and bolts in both existing slots. Opposed paths require suitable geometry. Release one accessible connection for inspection, leaving the plate tethered. Uses the tether parent alone, without guide, locating fence or contact stop.
openings.discriminator: If opposed paths stay taut and attachments resist sliding, retention should depend less on weak spare-plate magnetism. The ordinary magnetic rival may show greater spare displacement or earlier pull release. Either may fail; supplied 3 N versus 7 N pull checks do not establish stroke performance.
openings.probe: Inspect routing and measure wire needed against 0.5 m first. Proceed only with every segment, loop and anchor outside marked stroke clearance, marked 30 mm edge exposed and edge-free gloved handling. Never drill, cut, heat or glue plate/carriage; carriage stays attached to rails. Compare at most two configurations, tether versus magnets, with at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each. Final run uses spare; its removal uses thick gloves. Mark initial position; ruler measures translation and rotation-related corner displacement. Every observed displacement must be within 1 mm; removal/return within sixty seconds. Record pull release with 10 N scale where distinguishing. Defeat tether if loops slide, slack permits excess movement, opposed tension cannot be routed, handling exceeds sixty seconds or fabrication exceeds eighty minutes. Observation stays within twenty minutes; stop if informative measurements cannot fit.
openings.uncertainty: Slot positions/free routing dimensions are unspecified. Wire length, stiffness and reversible attachment capacity are unproved. Gloved bolt/loop manipulation without edge contact is assumed, not demonstrated.

lineage.reason: Retains tether-only relation, conditional comparison, defeats, uncertain fit, assumptions and resource stops.

decision: Check feasibility first, then bounded comparison. Recoverability does not establish retention; unsuccessful routing supports no feasible test or deployment claim. Supplied synthetic evidence only.
